RESULT (a2-saved-record-repair-diagnosis-20261023): the one registered offline diagnosis ran complete in 81.60 s of the 900 s (Tests row a2_saved_record_diagnosis PASS; no retry). The joined records show where the forecasts and the movements part, and one repair is proposed (not built). Read-only throughout: no training, no gate, no calibration relaxation, no checkpoint copy, nothing deleted; the duplicate original checkpoint is preserved.

RUN: three programs, each independently reviewed before the run (analysis 1cea4c53..., render dfc0d254..., pair 5e93d8e9...). The analysis ran complete in 64.3 s (576 of 576 arm fits, none failed); the render drew 15 of 15 pictures in 8.37 s. The existing arm fitter at c86363ae2 was used uncalibrated: cm and degrees, judged against no line.

1. JOINS AND GEOMETRY (item 1)
- All 9 counted captures and 72 of 72 outcomes joined to: the start joints (world record s - 1); the selected earlier goal (its world record in the preserved S4R_measure_496000 run: 72 of 72 verified and unique); the first and the selected command's forecasts (the planner's own score terms recomputed from the saved arrays: 72 of 72 within the reader's tolerance); the actual end (world record s + 4); and the command identity (the 25 body rows; the gaze row compared apart).
- Every start and end record is the nearest of its neighbours. The stored pose lags its record by one 5 ms physics substep. The movement allowance for that lag missed on 3 named records; they are reported, not counted as partial.
- Raw link and hinge discrepancies. The link reading is a forecast part's position in its parent's frame against the model's fixed offset; the elbow reading is its turn off the hinge axis.
  - upper-arm link median 1.02 cm (left) and 0.69 cm (right) on the first forecast; 1.13 and 0.71 cm on the selected; max 4.45 cm;
  - elbow off-axis median 3.56 and 3.71 degrees (first), 3.70 and 4.40 degrees (selected); max 30.7 degrees;
  - shoulder link median 0.26 to 0.29 cm;
  - the same readings on the measured end poses are about 1e-6 cm and degrees.
- IK/FK per-part residuals (the nearest legal arm, one start, uncalibrated): medians 0.26 to 0.97 cm and 0.29 to 3.68 degrees per part, first and selected alike.
- Numerical-fit status, kept apart:
  - the forecast fits met the fitter's stationarity line in 144 of 144 arms for each forecast;
  - the measured-end reference fits did not, in 94 and 98 of 144: the numerical floor that the fit-only correction addresses. Their residuals are a floor reading, not geometry.

2. SEARCH, OUTCOMES, PALMS (item 2)
- First versus selected, same body and goal (66 changed bodies):
  - the search lowered its predicted pose error in 66 of 66 (median -1.146 in the forecast's units);
  - the selected forecast was less consistent than the first in 36 (fit position total, median +0.21 cm), 37 (fit rotation total, +0.50 degrees), 38 (left elbow off-axis) and 43 (right elbow off-axis) of 66;
  - larger predicted gains came with larger additions (Spearman -0.35 and -0.39).
  So the search partly lowered its score by adding inconsistency. Most of the inconsistency was already in the first forecast.
- Predicted versus actual (changed bodies):
  - the selected forecast's end error was below the actual one by a median 0.634;
  - the actual end error fell below the start in 42 of 66;
  - the larger the predicted gain, the larger that miss (Spearman 0.30): the strongest relation measured.
  The arm inconsistency goes only weakly with the miss (Spearman 0.14 to 0.27). Bodies where the search added inconsistency ended worse than the start in 11 of 36; bodies where it removed inconsistency, in 13 of 30.
- Fallbacks (6): the first and selected forecasts are the same arrays. The actual end error rose in 5 of 6.
- Palm points (the hand body's origin) against the goal palm points:
  - the selected forecast was nearer than the first in 65 of 66 per arm;
  - the actual end was nearer than the start in 44 (left) and 36 (right) of 66;
  - the actual end was farther than the selected forecast in 36 (median 0.30 cm) and 38 (median 0.75 cm) of 66.
- 'Wrists toward in 45/72' is not a wrist count.
  - It is the reading's movement_toward_goal_cm, the body gap at the start minus at the end. The body gap is the mean distance in cm of the 25 non-gaze handles to the goal pose (read_pose_learning.py lines 657, 658 and 677; causal_chain.py lines 1856, 1858 and 1871 at 7dd0eabda). The denominator is the 72 usable outcomes, and the reading is above 0 in 45.
  - The palm points themselves: the left was nearer in 44, the right in 38, both in 25 and either in 57 of 72. The catalogue and the work record wording were corrected (d4f972b13).
- Not claimed: what the first command would have done (it was not executed), or causes (the correlations are descriptive).

3. CASE TABLE, EXAMPLES, ASSETS (item 3)
- Case table of all 72: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/h84/d1_planner_recovery/attempts/a2_record_diagnosis_d1/evidence/analysis/case_table.csv (also .json), plus a 28-column case_table_compact.csv.
- Examples. The selection rules are fixed in the program and recorded in the result under example_rules:
  - typical improving: plan step 496,340, body 1;
  - typical worsening: 496,300, body 6. It is a fallback, so its two forecasts are the same arrays;
  - largest disagreement: 496,280, body 5. The right palm point's selected forecast was 16.62 cm from its goal; the actual end was 23.63 cm away, against 19.48 cm at the start.
- 15 real MIMo renders: goal, start, first prediction, selected prediction and end; one camera per example; forecast parts left unconnected; the fitted arm drawn as an illustration only.
  - They are in the existing report asset group: docs/h84_body_repair_20261021/a2diag_<typical_improving|typical_worsening|largest_disagreement>_<1..5>_<goal|start|first_prediction|selected_prediction|end>.png.
  - Beside them: a2_diagnosis_provenance.json (renderer, hashes, cameras, printed numbers and checks) and a2_diagnosis_captions.txt (each path with its plain caption).
  - 16 of 16 copies equal their evidence files by sha256. Your HTML (last changed 3:09 AM PDT) and provenance.json (last changed Oct 22, 11:29 PM PDT) are untouched.
  - Inspected by eye: on the real panels the shoulder, elbow and palm-point markers sit on their body parts; labels are in the side columns; no caption carries a Check line.

4. ONE SMALLEST REPAIR (PROPOSED, not built): an arm-consistency lesson on the body head's existing tenure outputs.
- What: in efference_lesson, beside body_tenure (efference.py 1193-1197 at 7dd0eabda), on the same tenure output and achieved pose:
  - form the forecast poses as PhysicalGoalCost.forecast_pose does (physical_goal.py 104-110);
  - compute per arm, in torch, the readback's readings (check_arm_geometry_readback.py geometry, lines 479-498): the shoulder and upper-arm link residual vectors against the model's fixed offsets, the elbow's off-axis turn, the elbow angle beyond its range, and the forearm-to-hand distance beyond its reach;
  - express them in the forecast units (1.80 cm, 11.0 degrees), use the lesson's smooth L1 form, and sum them into efference_body.
- Producer: EfferenceHeads.body (efference.py 469-472), through forecast_pose. Consumers: the lesson (summed into the loss at lem_model.py 3604-3608) and the search's score and selection (physical_goal.py 15-23, 49-51, 58-59), which stay unchanged.
- What it changes: learning only, in the head's weights (the stored tenure latent is detached, efference.py 1240). Selection is unchanged, and there is no gate.
- Preservation: no new parameters and no shape change, so the efference module loads as saved (side modules load with strict=False, checkpoint.py 521-530); no EFFERENCE_VERSION change; saved worlds untouched.
- Cost: per command, B bodies x 2 arms x 5 readings of quaternion arithmetic on tensors already computed; no extra head forward. Its weight is measured first on the a2 saved forecasts, not chosen.
- Why not a joint-output/FK head now:
  - the inconsistency is already in the first forecast, before any search;
  - the search's additions are a median 0.21 cm and 0.50 degrees on top of it, so the defect sits in the head's outputs, where a lesson acts;
  - a joint-output/FK head would be needed if those additions dominated, since a lesson does not bound outputs far from training;
  - it would also need a torch arm forward kinematics (only the fingers have one: HandKinematics) and a changed final layer, which reinitializes the efference module on load.
- The physical measurement that settles it in the next learning block: the same joined readings on its captures.
  - The forecasts' upper-arm link and elbow off-axis readings, against the a2 baseline above, with the body_tenure error not rising.
  - The physical outcome: the actual end error below the start among changed commands (a2: 42 of 66), the forecast miss (a2: median -0.634), and the palm points' actual approach (a2: 44 and 36 of 66).
- Not addressed: the forecast's optimism under selection (Spearman 0.30), the strongest relation measured. The inconsistency goes only weakly with the misses, so this repair's effect on outcomes is unmeasured.

CORRECTION of my a2-bounded-arm-check-result-20261023: it said "a nonzero turn reads at least 1.49e-8 rad". That is wrong: the returned turn has no floor. True turns below about 1.5e-8 rad read exactly 0 (a dead zone), as the stationarity diagnosis measured (ik-stationarity-result-20261023).

IK BRANCH (your ik-numerical-correction-authorized-20261023): the fit-only correction is built (fdbc24bdf, compiled only) and under independent review, together with a corrected calibration driver. Its focused checks and ONE corrected calibration follow inside the 558.41 s, in their own consolidated result.

RECORDS: main commit b6009d602 holds the row's reading, the D1 work record a2_record_diagnosis_20261023, and the planner catalogue's two issues with the measured outcomes. Evidence: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/h84/d1_planner_recovery/attempts/a2_record_diagnosis_d1/evidence.

NEXT: your decision on the proposed repair. No training or experiment starts from this result.
